text:
elaine: quick one — Orbit Retail wants a tiny POC: SSE stream from our SDK, mid-stream tool call (product search), return structured JSON, then continue the text stream. they want copy-paste examples for their engs.

chris: two quick options: buffer-until-end (simpler) or chunked-result (stream large results). recommend chunked for inventory lists.

elaine: chunked sounds right. sample server snippet?

omar: minimal pseudo for chunked flow (server-side):
```py
# on tool_call_start: create buffer
# on tool_call_chunk: append
# on tool_result_chunk: emit SSE event {type:'tool_result_chunk', call_id, seq, text}
# on tool_result_end: emit {type:'tool_result_end', call_id'}
```

chris: client-side (browser) pattern: collect seq entries into array, when tool_result_end arrive join and JSON.parse. use is_base64 if payloads contain binary. keep seq as integer to handle reordering.

ops-bot: note: sample-client >=1.12 exposes helpers for emitting tool_result_chunk and tool_result_end.

elaine: security ask — temporary keys for POC and logs for tool payloads?

omar: give short-lived keys (30-60m) + TLS + IP allowlist. mark hosted POC outputs non-persistent; for any persistence use enterprise KMS. include request_id and call_id in logs for tracing.

chris: perf tip: batch_size=1 during debug; flip to smart batching for throughput in prod.

elaine: perfect. can one of you drop a tiny gist with server + browser examples and the 2-line security blurb? i'll add to the SOW.

omar: uploading gist now: https://gist.github.com/redwood/orbit-poc-streaming (includes run steps). security blurb: "POC keys are short-lived (recommended TTL 30-60 minutes). Streams use TLS and include request_id/call_id for audit. Do not persist tool outputs in hosted POC; use enterprise KMS for retained data."

elaine: cheers, putting this in the appendix :tada:
